why: The two inserted principles caused the scorer to avoid cut positions that would leave a tiny predicate-only right-hand fragment and to strongly downweight cuts whose following fragment looks likely to contradict; that moved many cuts away from verbs/complements (improving cohesion for longer pieces and reducing contradiction in the ≤7–≤99 bins). However, because the avoidance was implemented by shifting cuts leftward, it often pushed cuts into adjacent noun phrases and modifiers, producing many single-word or very-short left fragments and slightly hurting the shortest bins (≤3, ≤5), yielding an overall near-zero net change.
lesson: A follow-up edit should keep verbs with their complements and avoid high-contradiction right-hand fragments without simply shifting cuts into neighboring NPs or creating new one-word fragments (i.e., account for the symmetric effect on the left-hand fragment).
